the_stop.verdict: STOPPED. No src/ edit landed. This family is class (a) -- it authors two priced pair rows -- so umbrella Amendment L, Ruling 1's shape has something to stamp, and the slice was startable by the ruled act. It is the from-declaration PRICING STAGE that cannot carry it, in two independent ways, and amending that stage is an amendment's act and never a lane's: Amendment L, Ruling 3 budgeted the stage, Amendment M, Ruling 1 added its first missing term and Amendment N, Ruling 1 its second, each ruling in terms that it is not re-litigable by a lane. Amendment M, Ruling 1's own words name the two forbidden ways out and this slice took neither.
the_stop.why_the_census_did_not_catch_it: umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 2's term census is green -- 29 post-authoring packet-mutation sites, 0 uncovered, 3 static holder amps, 0 unfolded -- and it is green truthfully. Its predicate is a site that changes an ALREADY-AUTHORED packet's amount or its mitigation. Both terms below are applied while the packet is being authored, by the mitigation function the row is priced through, so no census in that shape can see them. That is recorded as a fact about the census's reach and not as a defect in it: Ruling 2 was written so terms would not be discovered one halt at a time, and this is a term of a kind its predicate does not range over.

blocker_1_the_basic_attack_delivery_term.what: This is the FIRST family to retire whose packet is delivered as a BASIC ATTACK SWING. Every family retired so far is priced by damage._mitigate and by nothing else, which is a resistance and the holder's own magic amp -- exactly the two terms survival.pricing.price_declared_packet carries. The bolt row is priced by damage._mitigate_basic_attack_swing, which applies three further terms after the resistance: the holder's basic amp (which the stage DOES carry, through StaticHolderAmps.factor_for at AttackClass.BASIC_ATTACK), the target's critical-strike damage multiplier, and damage._apply_target_basic_damage_reduction's plating multiplier and capped flat reduction.
blocker_1_the_basic_attack_delivery_term.which_of_them_are_foldable_and_which_is_: Two of the three are pure multipliers on a linear mitigation, so folding them into the declared pre-mitigation magnitude prices to the same real number -- the same argument the on_hit_strike retirement used for on-hit effectiveness. The third is not a multiplier at all. damage._apply_target_basic_damage_reduction subtracts min(flat, per_hit * cap) from the MITIGATED value, which is a capped flat subtraction and not a factor, and in the deterministic reading it is applied to the crit branch and the non-crit branch separately before they are blended, so the cap bites on one and not the other. There is no magnitude a declaration could state that reproduces it, and deriving one by dividing the pair engine's own price back out is the ratio path this stage exists to replace.
blocker_1_the_basic_attack_delivery_term.measured: Caitlyn at level 18 holding Runaan's Hurricane and Blade of the Ruined King, deterministic, one rotation at full auto uptime, roster_target_count 2 and roster_target_index 1, against the snapshot target. The pair engine's own state reads crit_chance 0.25, crit_multiplier 2.0, basic_amp 1.0, attack_damage 167, and the declaration's own compiled fields read secondary_damage_share 0.55 and secondary_max_targets 2.0, so the bolt's raw is 91.85000000000001 and the pre-mitigation blend is 114.8125. Priced at the fight's published effective armour of 50.0 that is 76.54166666666666, which is exactly the number the pair engine put on every one of the row's seven events -- so the from-declaration price reproduces the row EXACTLY while the three target-side terms are inert.
blocker_1_the_basic_attack_delivery_term.measured_with_the_terms_armed: Plated Steelcaps' declared plating multiplier of 0.9 moves the pair engine's per-hit figure to 68.88749999999999, which is 76.54166666666666 * 0.9 -- a pure factor. Randuin's Omen's declared critical-strike damage multiplier of 0.7 moves it to 67.35666666666665, which is the same blend with the crit branch scaled -- also foldable. Warden's Mail's declared Rock Solid, flat 15.0 capped at 0.2 of the instance, moves it to 63.60666666666666: the crit branch mitigates to 122.46666666666667 and loses the full 15.0, the non-crit branch mitigates to 61.233333333333334 and loses the capped 12.246666666666668, and 0.25 * 107.46666666666667 + 0.75 * 48.98666666666667 is 63.60666666666666. A walk pricing this family's declaration would have paid 76.54166666666666 against the pair engine's 63.60666666666666 -- 20.3 percent high on a leaf, which qualifies under R-15's first test.
blocker_1_the_basic_attack_delivery_term.reachability: All three are ordinary Summoner's Rift items an ENEMY may hold, and scenario.py:638-647 arms each of them on every pair fight against that enemy from the defender's own resolved defences. No committed coupled scenario arms any of them, which is precisely the shape umbrella Amendment N was written about: the R-20 line would have read a green zero over a population that could not contain the defect.

blocker_2_the_copied_on_hit_row_declares.what: The triage lists two authored pair rows for this family and only one of them is a packet this family's declaration states a magnitude for. secondary_Runaan's Hurricane is the bolt: a declared share of the attacker's damage, which is blocker 1's subject. on_hit_secondary_Runaan's Hurricane is the attack's on-hit effects COPIED onto the bolt's target, and damage._copied_on_hit_packet builds it out of on_hits.static_on_hit_by_type -- an already-MITIGATED aggregate -- plus a per-application _mitigate of every current-health strike against the secondary target's own falling health.
blocker_2_the_copied_on_hit_row_declares.why_that_is_a_ruling_and_not_an_arithmet: The runaans_hurricane.secondary_target rule declares exactly two numbers, max_targets and damage_share, and neither is a magnitude for that row. The magnitudes are the on_hit_strike family's own declarations, delivered at a second subject: measured on the probe above, the copied row's seven events read 80.0, 56.55166666666666, 39.507333333333335, 22.799639999999997, 11.981787733333329, 3.333333333333333 and 3.333333333333333, against Blade of the Ruined King's own row carrying declarations of 120.0, 106.85, 94.22599999999998, 82.10695999999997, 70.47268159999997, 59.30377433599999 and 48.58162336255999 for the same seven applications. Declaring those magnitudes under runaans_hurricane.secondary_target would make the walk price a retired family's declarations a second time under another family's mechanic, and D-62's key is (mechanic, subject, event_id) -- which is exactly the question of which family owns the number, a D-60 question a lane may not answer.
blocker_2_the_copied_on_hit_row_declares.the_previous_lane_already_deferred_it: The on_hit_strike retirement measured this same row and refused to stamp it, recording that it 'carries a different packet to a second target and belongs to the secondary_target family, whose deferral still stands'. That refusal was correct and it is not an answer: it says which family's slice owns the row, not what that slice may declare for it.

what_this_slice_refused.fold_the_price_back_out: Declaring a magnitude derived by dividing the pair engine's own mitigated figure by its mitigation is the ratio path the from-declaration stage exists to replace, and umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 1 forbids the same move for the resistance term in terms.
what_this_slice_refused.refuse_the_packet_when_a_term_is_armed: Amendment M, Ruling 1's second forbidden shape: refusing a packet whose holder has an amp armed deletes the number in the other direction, which is worse than the ratio path it replaces because that path at least refuses by name. The same reading applies to a target-side term.
what_this_slice_refused.retire_half_the_family: Stamping the bolt row and leaving the copied row unstamped would leave one of the family's two authored rows priced by the pair engine and the other by the walk, which is neither half of Amendment L, Ruling 1 and is not a smaller version of it.
what_this_slice_refused.add_the_term_to_the_pricing_stage: Amendment L, Ruling 3 budgets that stage and Amendments M and N amend it, each ruling that it is not re-litigable by a lane. A basic-attack delivery term is a fourth amendment to it, and inventing one here is what Amendment N's closing sentence removes the excuse for.

no_baseline_moves: R-32's five baselines are untouched by every commit of this slice, and so is src/. The only artifacts that move are this receipt, the rulings ledger and the gap ledger.
the_ruling_that_settled_it: Umbrella Amendment R, 2026-08-16, and it answers BOTH halves this receipt refused to answer for itself. RULING 1, the swing terms: the from-declaration pricing stage gains the basic-attack swing composition -- mitigation at the packet's own resistance, the holder's static amps pre-mitigation, then the target-side terms -- of which the target's critical-strike damage multiplier and the plating multiplier FOLD, exactly as this receipt measured them to, and Warden's Mail's Rock Solid is NEVER folded. min(flat, per_hit * cap) is carried as a term of its own, the flat, its cap and its instance count transported on the declaration and subtracted per branch before the deterministic blend, because a subtraction is not a factor. The term rides ON the declaration, transported from the authored ledger rather than resolved again at the walk, and a declaration no swing delivered carries none and prices exactly as it prices today. RULING 3, the copied row: secondary_target is a ROUTING family that re-delivers SOURCE families' declared magnitudes at a second subject and declares no magnitude of its own -- so the copied packet prices from the source family's declaration composed with the router's declared damage_share, attributed under D-62 at (source mechanic, secondary subject, event_id), with the routing recorded in provenance, and runaans_hurricane.secondary_target goes on declaring exactly max_targets and damage_share. Two rulings ride beside them and both were opened by this receipt's own measurements: RULING 2 widens Amendment N, Ruling 2's term census to authoring-time mitigation terms, recording this receipt's census paragraph as truthful under the old predicate rather than as a defect found in it; RULING 4 orders the covering scenario this receipt said was owed, as an integration act reading a derived term mapping.
what_the_ruling_measured_differently_fro: One sentence of this receipt is wrong and the ruling records it rather than editing it. Under blocker 1's reachability heading this receipt says no committed coupled scenario arms any of the three target-side terms. Measured on the ruling's own commit by running every pair fight of every committed coupled scenario with the defender-state hand-off instrumented, exactly one scenario does: immolate_active_bruiser_roster arms a plating multiplier of 0.9 and a critical-strike damage multiplier of 0.7 on its Darius main as DEFENDER, in two pair fights, because roster_composition.target_overrides hands a defender's resolved state to every pair fight the walk runs and that scenario is attacked as well as attacking. Warden's Mail's Rock Solid -- the one term that actually blocks -- is armed by no committed coupled scenario and by no bench roster at all. So the qualified sentence this receipt wrote into its rulings-owed row is the correct one: what nothing arms is a swing term on a defender a basic-attack ROUTER attacks, which is the two-sided join Ruling 4 makes the coverage derivation read. The correction changes nothing about the stop: the blocking term is unarmed either way, and the figures this receipt measured on its own probe all reproduce exactly.
what_this_receipt_owes_next: Nothing that a ruling has to buy, and one slice that budget now buys. secondary_target/receipt_walk stands OPEN and overdue with its population unchanged at 3498 and its triage class (a) intact -- Amendment R retires nothing and reads the debt as no smaller -- but the row is startable by the ruled act for the first time: Amendment L, Ruling 1's shape has two rows to stamp, and the pricing stage now has a ruled composition for both of them. Two prerequisites land in front of the retirement rather than inside it. Ruling 4's covering scenario is an INTEGRATION act (R-12, R-32) and a baseline moves in the integration agent's own commit, never inside the semantic slice; and Ruling 2's widened census is a gate the retirement runs under, which is what keeps the next term from being found the way this one was. The four figures below are the fixture SEEDS by their predicate; what binds numerically is what the fixture's own instrument produces.
what_stands_unedited: Every number, the verdict, the enumerated population of 3498, the four refused ways out and both blockers stand exactly as filed, including the reachability sentence the ruling measured differently -- the correction is recorded beside it and not in place of it, which is how an answered question stays joined to the question that was asked. `decisions` is not extended either: that list is what the slice landed against, and an amendment dated after the slice stopped is not something it landed against. The one edit to a standing field is its name -- what_stands_after_the_stop.the_ruling_it_owes now reads the_ruling_it_owed_when_it_was_filed, because a receipt with two answers to one question answers neither.
